PM Carney’s January 14–17, 2026, trip to Beijing marked the first visit by a Canadian Prime Minister to China since 2017, aimed at resetting “complex” bilateral ties after nearly a decade of tension [2][3][4]. The visit produced a **preliminary landmark trade agreement** to reduce Chinese tariffs on Canadian canola from 84% to 15% by March 1, while allowing approximately 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles into Canada at a 6.1% levy [10][11], alongside five new memorandums of understanding covering agriculture, crime combat, and cultural exchanges [10][14]. PM Carney publicly announced these outcomes during a media availability on January 16 and delivered opening remarks at a Canada China Business Council gala dinner [10][17].
